pages.x: Spain had become a republic in 1931, and it was split between left and right, town and country, the Church and its enemies. In February 1936 a left-wing Popular Front won the elections. In July a group of generals, among them Francisco Franco, rose in revolt, and the country split in two.

Franco flew to Morocco to lead Spain's colonial army, and German and Italian planes carried his troops over the sea to Spain, the first big airlift in history. His Nationalists, backed by the Church, landowners and fascists, began a slow conquest, shooting tens of thousands of their enemies behind the lines.

In November 1936 Franco's army reached the edge of Madrid. Its people, with the first foreign volunteers, held the city under the slogan they shall not pass, and it held out until the very end of the war.

Hitler and Mussolini sent Franco planes, tanks and soldiers, and Stalin armed the Republic. Some 35,000 volunteers from over 50 countries came to fight for the Republic in the International Brigades, and others, like the writer George Orwell, joined its militias. Both sides killed civilians; in Republican areas thousands of priests and nuns were murdered.

On 26 April 1937 German and Italian bombers attacked the Basque town of Guernica on market day and left it in flames. Pablo Picasso, in Paris, painted a huge black, white and grey picture of screaming women, a dying horse and a bull. Guernica became the most famous protest against war ever painted.

The Republic's side was torn by feuds between communists, socialists and anarchists, and Franco's better armed forces slowly won. Barcelona fell in January 1939 and Madrid in March. Half a million Republicans fled over the mountains to France, many to be held in camps on the beaches.
Franco ruled Spain as a dictator until his death in 1975. Tens of thousands of his opponents were executed after the war, and hundreds of thousands passed through prisons and camps.
pages.of: died in the war and the killings

pages.x: The war was a rehearsal for the Second World War, a testing ground for German and Italian bombers and tanks. Spain became a democracy again after Franco's death, and it still argues about how to remember the war and its mass graves.
pts: Began with a generals' revolt in July 1936
